solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: What’s sandwiched between labels, spinning? (7)

blocks.note: the surface wants a filling between stickers; the setter means the material of an old record, with a paper label on each face
the surface wants something twirling; the setter means a 78 turning on a gramophone

annotation.surface: A riddle about something caught between two stickers and going round.
annotation.walkthrough: Old 78 rpm records were pressed in shellac, so the material sits between the paper label on each side as the disc spins on the turntable.
annotation.definitionFit: Shellac is the resin that 78 rpm gramophone records were made from.

entries.clue: Scary fish under tree in burn (5-8)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue the fish sits below the rest
indicatorNotes.in: the tree goes inside the word for burn

blocks.note: a sting is a burning pain
the conifer, placed inside STING after its S
a ling is a sea fish of the cod family

annotation.surface: A frightening fish lurking beneath a tree beside a Scottish stream.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burn' reads as a Scottish stream, which suits the fish and the tree; here it means the verb for a sharp pain.
annotation.definitionFit: Something spine-tingling is thrilling or frightening, so scary.

entries.clue: Go around rear of shop and look for milk (7)

indicatorNotes.around: the word for go is wrapped round the other pieces
indicatorNotes.rear of: take only the last letter of shop

blocks.note: to exit is to go out
last letter of shop
lo = look! as in 'lo and behold'

annotation.surface: An instruction to nip round the back of the shop to find some milk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look for milk' reads as a shopping errand; 'milk' is a verb meaning to take advantage of.
annotation.definitionFit: To milk someone or something is to exploit it for all it is worth.

entries.clue: Fool can accept losing you (5)

indicatorNotes.losing: the word for accept drops the letter standing for you

blocks.note: can and loo are both slang for a toilet
BUY (accept, as in 'I don't buy that') without U, the textspeak you

annotation.surface: A fool is able to accept losing you as a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning is able to; it is the noun, a toilet. U standing for 'you' is a standard crossword swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A looby is an old word for a clumsy, stupid person, a fool.

entries.clue: Two coppers ask criminal about drug — something small consumed at parties? (8)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters of ask are rearranged
indicatorNotes.about: those rearranged letters go around the drug

blocks.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper, PC is a police constable
ASK rearranged
E = ecstasy, placed inside AKS

annotation.surface: Police officers question a criminal about drugs being taken at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drugs bust at a party, which makes 'something small consumed' look like a pill; the question mark admits the cake is the innocent reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Cupcakes are small individual cakes, typical party food.

entries.clue: Refuse to acknowledge broadcast following U-turn of papers (6)

indicatorNotes.U-turn of: a U-turn sends the word for papers back the other way
indicatorNotes.following: the word for broadcast comes after

blocks.note: ID (identity papers) turned round
seed broadcast is scattered, or sown

annotation.surface: A government refusing to admit to a news broadcast after its newspapers backtracked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio or television; it is the old farming sense of scattering seed by hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to disown a child or a remark is to deny any connection with it.

entries.clue: Manage to obtain alcoholic drink during party (4,2)

indicatorNotes.during: the drink comes in the middle of the party

blocks.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
placed inside DUP after its D

annotation.surface: Someone manages to get hold of a stiff drink while at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a celebration, which suits the drink; it is the political party. The DUP is a Northern Irish unionist party.
annotation.definitionFit: To drum up support or custom is to manage to obtain it by effort.

entries.clue: Group periodically saying heartless command (9)

indicatorNotes.periodically: take every other letter of saying
indicatorNotes.heartless: the middle letter of the word for command is removed

blocks.note: S, Y and N, the first, third and fifth letters of saying
DICTATE without its central T

annotation.surface: A group periodically issues a harsh order.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first three odd letters of 'saying' are needed; the rest of the word is dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of people or firms combined for a shared purpose.

entries.clue: Side retains cup status following European match (7)

indicatorNotes.retains: the word for side holds the other pieces inside
indicatorNotes.following: the cup size comes after the European

blocks.note: a wing is a side of a building or a team
standard abbreviation
DD is a bra cup size

annotation.surface: A football team keeps its standing in a cup competition after a European tie.
annotation.walkthrough: Cup, side and match all point to football; the cup is a bra cup and the match is a marriage.
annotation.definitionFit: Match in its old sense of a marriage; the ceremony that seals one stands in for it by association.

entries.clue: Unrehearsed dance exercises welcomed by Greek character on island (9)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: the Greek letter takes the dance and exercises inside it
indicatorNotes.on: that whole piece is placed next to the island

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the Greek letter M, wrapped round the next two pieces
a prom is a formal school dance
PT = physical training

annotation.surface: An unrehearsed dance routine greeted by a Greek on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dance' sits beside 'Unrehearsed' as if describing it; it is PROM, and 'Unrehearsed' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done without preparation, unrehearsed.

entries.clue: Bent and bared firm bottom (5)

indicatorNotes.Bent: the letters of and are twisted into a new order
indicatorNotes.bared: firm is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: AND rearranged
FIRM without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone bends over and shows a firm bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a cheeky mooning; 'bottom' is not a rear end but the lowest point.
annotation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, its bottom.

entries.clue: Member of church choir not calm, excited about start of Alleluia! (5,8)

indicatorNotes.excited: the letters are stirred up into a new order
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters come around the extra A
indicatorNotes.start of: take only the first letter of Alleluia

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
first letter, joining the fodder

annotation.surface: A church chorister gets worked up at the first Alleluia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member of church choir' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'church', and 'choir' starts the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by membership: the church meant is the one headed by the Pope, and its followers take its name.

entries.clue: Some say no before going round wood (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: the answer is part of the following words

blocks.note: saY NO BEfore read right to left

annotation.surface: Some people refuse before a trip around the woods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Going round wood' sounds like a walk in the forest; 'going round' turns the letters back, and 'wood' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard, dark tropical wood.

entries.clue: Element of clue uncovered in a note about Duck’s second offering? (9)

indicatorNotes.in: those letters go inside the rest
indicatorNotes.about: the note wraps round the letter from Duck
indicatorNotes.second: take the second letter of Duck

blocks.note: as written
CLUE without its first and last letters
a minim is a half note in music
second letter of Duck, placed inside MINIM

annotation.surface: A question about a scrap of a clue and what a cricketer out for a duck might offer next.
annotation.walkthrough: The British spelling is needed: ALUMINIUM, with the extra I, is what the letters give.
annotation.definitionFit: Aluminium is a chemical element, the light silvery metal.

entries.clue: One competitor moving east in corporate system (8)

indicatorNotes.moving east: on a map east is to the right, so the E shifts rightwards in the word

blocks.note: I = one, the Roman numeral
ENTRANT with its leading E moved two places to the right

annotation.surface: A rival relocating eastwards within a company's structure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moving east' reads as a transfer to another office; in an across answer it pushes the letter E towards the right.
annotation.definitionFit: An intranet is a private computer network within a company.

entries.clue: Morning mist envelops thoroughfare in city (9)

indicatorNotes.envelops: the word for mist surrounds the thoroughfare

blocks.note: am = before noon
steam is a mist of water vapour
RD = road, placed inside STEAM

annotation.surface: Early morning fog hangs over a street in a city.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a weather report; the city in it is not scenery but the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dutch capital is one instance of a city.

entries.clue: Rabbit’s just perfect (4,2)

blocks.note: to rabbit is British slang for talking tediously at length
British informal for exactly right, spot on

annotation.surface: Someone declares their pet rabbit to be simply perfect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal; in British slang to rabbit, or to bang on, is to talk at tedious length.
annotation.definitionFit: Bang on is British informal for exactly right, just perfect.

entries.clue: Forget about sardonic nob on the radio (5,3)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: a radio carries sound only, so the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: wry = sardonic; a toff is a British word for a posh person, a nob

annotation.surface: A mocking aristocrat on a radio programme ought to be ignored.
annotation.walkthrough: A toff, like a nob, is British slang for an upper-class person; say WRY TOFF quickly and it becomes WRITE OFF.
annotation.definitionFit: To write off a loss or a person is to forget about it as a lost cause.

entries.clue: Duke in difficulty knocked over king’s port (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the duke goes inside the word for difficulty
indicatorNotes.knocked over: that combination is toppled and read backwards

blocks.note: a snag is a problem
standard abbreviation, placed inside SNAG to make SNADG
chess notation

annotation.surface: A duke in trouble topples a king's seaport.
annotation.walkthrough: The Duke goes into SNAG after the A, and the whole is read backwards before the king is added.
annotation.definitionFit: Gdańsk is a major Baltic port in northern Poland.

entries.clue: Records kept are to include chapter four (7)

indicatorNotes.to include: are takes the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: as written, split around the rest
the usual abbreviation for chapter, as in book references
Roman numeral

annotation.surface: Some records are said to contain a fourth chapter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Records kept are' reads as one sentence; the definition is 'Records kept', and 'are' is the outer shell of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names both stored historical documents and the place that keeps them.

entries.clue: Drink welcome around noon — relax at regular intervals (5,3)

indicatorNotes.around: the word for welcome surrounds noon
indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: take every second letter of relax

blocks.note: to greet is to welcome
N = noon, placed inside GREET
the second and fourth letters of relax

annotation.surface: A welcome drink at lunchtime, and a chance to unwind now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like an instruction to follow the welcome; it is the definition, and a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: tea brewed from unfermented leaves is one kind of drink.

entries.clue: Eject four drunken university bores time after time (4,3)

indicatorNotes.drunken: the letters stagger into a new order
indicatorNotes.bores: the rearranged letters drill into the gap between the two times

blocks.note: T = time, the first of two
FOUR plus U (university), rearranged
the second T

annotation.surface: Four drunk students bore people over and over until they are thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bores' reads as being tedious, which suits drunk students; it means drills into, so the anagram goes between the two Ts.
annotation.definitionFit: To turf out is British informal for to eject someone.

entries.clue: Year and a month to climb outside of large tower (6)

indicatorNotes.to climb: in a down answer, climbing means the letters read upwards
indicatorNotes.outside of: the month sits around the letter for large

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
February, wrapped round L to make FLEB
L = large, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: A year and a month spent climbing the outside of a big tower.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer, climbing means reading from the bottom up, so the pieces are assembled in reverse before they are entered.
annotation.definitionFit: A belfry is a bell tower, or the room in one that houses the bells.

entries.clue: In protecting M’s predecessor, Bond’s not fair? (9)

indicatorNotes.protecting: the word for bond shelters the letter inside it
indicatorNotes.predecessor: the letter that comes just before M in the alphabet

blocks.note: as written
cement bonds things together
L precedes M in the alphabet; placed inside CEMENT after the C

annotation.surface: A Bond film complaint: shielding M's predecessor isn't fair on him.
annotation.walkthrough: M, Bond and predecessor all point to the spy films; M is just the letter, and 'Bond' is glue.
annotation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is not fair: stormy or harsh.

entries.clue: Branch where one may settle one’s bill? (5)

annotation.definition: Branch where one may settle one’s bill?

blocks.note: the surface wants a bank branch; the setter means a tree branch where a bird settles
the surface wants an invoice to pay; the setter means a bird's beak

annotation.surface: A bank branch where you can go and pay what you owe.
annotation.walkthrough: The branch is a tree branch, not a bank, and the bill is a bird's beak: a perched bird settles its bill.
annotation.definitionFit: A perch is a branch or bar where a bird rests.

entries.clue: Staple page together with a street map on the inside (5)

indicatorNotes.on the inside: take only the letter at the centre of map

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
as written
standard abbreviation
middle letter of map

annotation.surface: Instructions for stapling a page to a street map inside a booklet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staple' reads as the verb for fastening pages; it is the noun, a basic foodstuff.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasta is a staple food in Italy and far beyond.

entries.clue: Crush spirit, overcoming resistance with decisiveness at the front (5)

indicatorNotes.overcoming: the spirit sits over, and so around, the resistance
indicatorNotes.at the front: take the first letter of decisiveness

blocks.note: the spirit drink
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, placed inside GIN
first letter of decisiveness

annotation.surface: A rallying call to crush the enemy's morale by overcoming their resistance with decisive leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crush spirit' reads as breaking morale; the spirit is GIN, and 'Crush' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To grind something is to crush it into small pieces.

entries.clue: Piece of furniture’s too soft, rickety and almost antique (9)

indicatorNotes.rickety: the letters wobble into a new order
indicatorNotes.almost: drop the last letter of the word for antique

blocks.note: TOO SOFT rearranged
OLD without its last letter

annotation.surface: A dealer's verdict on a chair: too soft, wobbly and nearly an antique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' reads as a description of the furniture, which is exactly what it would be in the surface; here it stirs the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool for resting the feet, a piece of furniture.

entries.clue: Suitable space left in empty salvage yard (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the space and left go inside the other pieces
indicatorNotes.empty: salvage is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: salvage with its middle removed
an em is a printer's space
standard abbreviation
Y = yard, the unit of length

annotation.surface: A decent patch of ground left free in an otherwise bare scrapyard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salvage yard' reads as one place; the setter splits it, so only 'salvage' is emptied and 'yard' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: conduct that is fitting for the occasion.

entries.clue: Desperate country’s short — it’s embroiled in recession (7)

indicatorNotes.short: the country loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.embroiled in: the turned word goes inside the shortened country

blocks.note: FRANCE without its last letter
the word it, taken as written with its 's dropped
IT goes backwards to TI, inside FRANC after FRAN

annotation.surface: A country short of money and caught up in an economic downturn is getting desperate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recession' reads as an economic slump, which fits the struggling country; it tells IT to go backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Frantic means desperate, wild with worry or hurry.
